sn56.14:3.2: It’s the craving that leads to future lives, mixed up with relishing and greed, taking pleasure there wherever it alights. That is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for nonexistence—
sn56.14:3.3: This is called the noble truth of the origin of suffering.
sn56.14:4.2: It’s the fading away and cessation of that very same craving no residue left behind; giving it away, letting it go, releasing it, and not clinging to it—
sn56.14:4.3: This is called the noble truth of the cessation of suffering.
sn56.14:5.4: This is called the noble truth of the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.
sn56.14:5.5: These are the four noble truths.
